correctness.rationale: For a nonzero \(F\)-linear map \(t:E\to E\) on a quadratic field extension, rank two makes \(t\) surjective and the trace-algebra axiom forces multiplication by \(t(1)\). Rank one gives image \(Fz\); applying the axiom at a nonzero image element forces \(z\in F^\times\), so the map is an arbitrary nonzero functional \(E\to F\). Conversely every such functional satisfies the axiom. In a purely inseparable quadratic extension the field trace is zero, so these functionals are not \(x\mapsto\operatorname{Tr}(cx)\). The explicit \(F_2(s)\subset F_2(s)(u)\), \(u^2=s\), example checks directly.

correctness.rationale: For a quadratic field extension, the trace-algebra axiom and the rank of the F-linear map give an exhaustive dichotomy: rank two forces multiplication by t(1), while rank one forces the image to be F and hence gives an arbitrary nonzero functional E→F. The classical trace-pairing criterion then shows that the source's Tr(cx) parametrization is exhaustive exactly in the separable case and collapses to zero in the inseparable case.
